# HIMLoco quadruped robot motion control: From paper understanding to reproduction in Isaac Lab new stack

Further reading: [ From Isaac Gym to Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab: Migration experience sharing ](02-migration-experience-sharing.md), covering version troubleshooting, task mapping, observation timing, terminated sample processing, and video acceptance.

This chapter guides you through an engineering-based learning experience with HIMLoco: first, understand what the ICLR 2024 paper **Hybrid Internal Model: Learning Agile Legged Locomotion with Simulated Robot Response** aims to solve, then examine the open-source repository to clarify the observations, internal model, PPO training, and Sim2Real design. Finally, migrate the training process that originally relied on Isaac Gym Preview 4 to the new Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab environment, and run the smoke test on Blackwell GPU.

The goal of this chapter is not to train a paper-level final policy, but to help everyone understand the most critical engineering processes first:

- Why HIMLoco is not an ordinary `obs -> action` PPO;
- Where the historical observations of `45 x 6 = 270` and `238`'s privileged critic observation come from;
- How `HIMEstimator` learns speed and hidden variables from historical proprioception;
- Why the old Isaac Gym stack fails on Blackwell GPU;
- How to run tasks and HIM algorithms using the new Isaac Lab / PyTorch CUDA 12.8 stack;
- What is the relationship between the official demo video, local rendering video, and complete training results;
- What smoke tests can prove, and what they cannot prove.

> Note: The reproduction in this chapter uses the open-source repository [ OpenRobotLab/HIMLoco](https://github.com/OpenRobotLab/HIMLoco), the paper project page is [ the official HIMLoco homepage](https://junfeng-long.github.io/HIMLoco/), and the paper is [ arXiv:2312.11460](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11460). The README of the official repository indicates that the training code is available, but the deployment guide is not yet available. Therefore, this chapter focuses on the training pipeline, algorithm structure, and migration to the new Isaac Lab stack, without interpreting the smoke test results as the real robot deployment being completed.

## Reproduction Roadmap

You can view this chapter as a reinforcement learning experiment class for quadruped robots. We start from the original paper and repository to understand why the author designed the Hybrid Internal Model. Then, we examine how each tensor flows in the engineering implementation. Finally, we complete the minimum training and validation using the local migration version task.

| Phase | Main Goal | Success Sign | Priority Checks When Failing |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1. Understand the policy | Comprehend the relationship between HIM, privileged critic, and history observation | Ability to explain why the actor uses only deployable observations | Avoid getting stuck on all reward details first |
| 2. Read the original repository | Locate the code locations for environment, algorithm, runner, and estimator | Ability to locate `him_ppo.py` and `him_estimator.py` | Confirm the use of `rsl_rl` modified within the repository |
| 3. Verify the old stack | Set up the Isaac Gym Preview 4 environment | `train.py --help` runs successfully | Python 3.7/3.8, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` |
| 4. Blackwell troubleshooting | Determine if old PyTorch/CUDA support the current GPU | Detect `sm_120` is incompatible with the old wheel | `torch.cuda.get_arch_list()` |
| 5. Isaac Lab migration | Register new tasks and runners | policy observation `270`, critic observation `238` | Isaac Lab path, task entry point |
| 6. HIM smoke test | Run 64 environments, 2 iterations successfully | Generate loss, fps, checkpoint files | Observation set, batch shape, CUDA version |
| 7. Rendering verification | Record a video of the Isaac Lab training process | Can see A1 being advanced through rough terrain simulation | Do not treat short-step random policies as convergent步态 |

It is necessary to clarify the significance of the smoke test: it proves that environment creation, observation construction, action execution, reward calculation, rollout storage, backpropagation, and optimizer update all work properly. It does not prove that the policy has converged, nor does it indicate that the model can be directly deployed on a real robot.

## 1. What problem does HIMLoco solve

In quadruped robot motion control, reinforcement learning policies often face a contradiction: simulation tools possess many information that real robots cannot obtain during deployment, such as accurate base linear velocity, external disturbances, terrain height, contact states, and changes in rigid body mass. However, when using a real robot, the policy usually relies only on IMU, joint encoders, previous action, and a small amount of state estimation.

If the actor directly reads these simulation privileges during training, the policy will look good in the simulation. However, when deployed, the information is missing, making Sim2Real vulnerable. If these information are completely omitted, the simulation can be wasted by using the supervision signals it provides for training.

The core idea of HIMLoco is to build a bridge between the two:

- During training, the critic can use privileged observations to help PPO learn a more accurate value function;
- The actor does not directly read privileged observations, but only the historical proprioception that is likely to be obtained in real deployment;
- An additional `HIMEstimator` is trained to infer the base velocity and latent hidden variables from historical observations;
- Finally, the actor uses `当前观测 + 估计速度 + latent` to output 12 joint actions.

In other words, HIMLoco does not let the policy "peek at the answers," but instead trains an internal model so that the robot can infer the current dynamics state from its own historical responses.

## II. Code organization in the original repository

The HIMLoco open-source repository is based on modifications of `legged_gym` and `rsl_rl`. When reading the code, do not use the original `legged_gym` or `rsl_rl` for installation comparison, as the author has added special runners, storage, actor-critic, and PPO for HIM within the repository.

The core directory can be understood as follows:

| Path | Function |
| :-- | :-- |
| `legged_gym/legged_gym/envs/base/legged_robot.py` | Base class for quadruped robot environments, responsible for simulation of step, reward, termination, and observation |
| `legged_gym/legged_gym/envs/a1/a1_config.py` | Initial pose, PD parameters, reward weights, and command range for Unitree A1 |
| `legged_gym/legged_gym/scripts/train.py` | Training entry point, used to create the environment and runner |
| `legged_gym/legged_gym/scripts/play.py` | Test and TorchScript export entry point |
| `rsl_rl/rsl_rl/runners/him_on_policy_runner.py` | Main HIM training loop |
| `rsl_rl/rsl_rl/algorithms/him_ppo.py` | PPO update and estimator update |
| `rsl_rl/rsl_rl/modules/him_actor_critic.py` | Combined network of actor, critic, and estimator |
| `rsl_rl/rsl_rl/modules/him_estimator.py` | Internal model estimator and self-supervised loss |
| `rsl_rl/rsl_rl/storage/him_rollout_storage.py` | Rollout buffer for saving the next privileged observation |

The training entry itself is very short:

```python
env, env_cfg = task_registry.make_env(name=args.task, args=args)
ppo_runner, train_cfg = task_registry.make_alg_runner(env=env, name=args.task, args=args)
ppo_runner.learn(num_learning_iterations=train_cfg.runner.max_iterations, init_at_random_ep_len=True)
```

True logic lies in the environment and runner created by the registry. When reading the code, you can follow the order of "the environment generates tensors first, and the runner consumes them later", and avoid getting stuck in the PPO formula from the beginning.

## III. How the observation tensor flows

The observation design in HIMLoco is the most valuable part of the entire paper and repository. It separates the information visible to the actor from that visible to the critic.

### 1. one-step observation of actor

Each frame of actor observation in the original repository has 45 dimensions:

| Component | Dimension | Meaning |
| :-- | --: | :-- |
| command | 3 | Target x/y speed and yaw speed |
| base angular velocity | 3 | Angular velocity in the body frame |
| projected gravity | 3 | Projection of gravity in the body frame, used to represent posture |
| joint position error | 12 | Difference between the current joint position and the default joint position |
| joint velocity | 12 | Joint velocity |
| last action | 12 | Action at the previous moment |
| Total | 45 | Single-frame proprioception |

Then HIMLoco stacks 6 frames of history:

```text
actor observation = 45 x 6 = 270
```

This is similar to the “short-term memory” on a robot. Single-frame proprioception may not be able to accurately determine speed, delay, contact, and external disturbances, but 6 frames of history allow the network to infer these states from the response trends.

### 2. Critic's privileged observation

critic uses 238-dimensional privileged observation:

| Component | Dimension | Meaning |
| :-- | --: | :-- |
| one-step actor observation | 45 | Consistent with the actor's current frame observations |
| base linear velocity | 3 | Directly provided by the simulator; usually unreliable in real robot deployment |
| external force | 3 | External disturbance forces in simulation |
| height scan | 187 | Height sampling of the terrain around the body |
| Total | 238 | Special privileges for critic / estimator training |

The design here is a typical asymmetric actor-critic approach: the actor simulates deployment constraints, while the critic uses simulation true values to reduce training difficulty.

### 3. The HIM actor actually consumes 64 dimensions

Many people think that the input of actor MLP is 270 dimensions when they first see the code, but it isn't. `HIMEstimator` First, encode the 270-dimensional historical observations as:

```text
estimated base velocity: 3
latent: 16
```

Then the input for actor MLP is:

```text
当前 one-step obs 45
+ estimated base velocity 3
+ latent 16
= 64
```

This is the form in which the "internal model" of HIMLoco appears in the code.

<p align="center">
  <img src="../../../05-具身场景的深度和强化学习/02HIMLoco-IsaacLab复现/assets/him_tensor_flow.svg" width="96%" alt="HIMLoco 张量流示意图">
</p>

**Figure 3: HIMLoco’s tensor flow.** This figure is a reproduction version of the data flow organized in this chapter based on the source code. Note that the inputs of the actor and critic are different: the actor obtains its internal state from historical observations via the estimator, while the critic directly reads the privileged observations during training.

## IV. Training Objectives of the Estimator

`HIMEstimator` is not just an ordinary encoder. It has two training objectives:

1. Predict the base linear velocity;
2. Learn structured latent through swap loss in prototype/Sinkhorn style.

The key segment in the code is:

```python
vel = next_critic_obs[:, self.num_one_step_obs:self.num_one_step_obs+3].detach()
next_obs = next_critic_obs.detach()[:, 3:self.num_one_step_obs+3]
```

Here, `vel` comes from the real base linear velocity in next privileged observation, serving as a supervisory signal for the estimator. `next_obs` is used by the target network to generate a latent target. Subsequently, the code will calculate:

```python
estimation_loss = F.mse_loss(pred_vel, vel)
swap_loss = -0.5 * (q_s * log_p_t + q_t * log_p_s).mean()
```

For robot learning, this design is very insightful: it doesn’t just let the policy track the reward end-to-end, but incorporates an interpretable intermediate task within the policy, enabling the network to learn how to estimate dynamic quantities that are difficult to measure directly during deployment.

## 5. Why the original Isaac Gym stack doesn't work on new graphics cards

The recommended environment for the official README is:

```text
Ubuntu 20.04
Python 3.7.16
PyTorch 1.10.0+cu113
Isaac Gym Preview 4
```

This environment is reasonable for old graphics cards, but a CUDA architecture mismatch occurs with the Blackwell GPU. Our tested graphics card is `NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition`, and its compute capability is `sm_120`. PyTorch 1.10.0+cu113 only supports older architectures, which results in errors during training:

```text
CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device
```

We also tried using the newer PyTorch 2.4.1+cu124 under Python 3.8, which is one of the higher Python versions that the Isaac Gym Preview 4 binding can tolerate. However, the `torch.cuda.get_arch_list()` in this wheel only goes up to `sm_90`, and it cannot cover `sm_120`.

Therefore, for the Blackwell route, a more reliable approach is not to continue fixing Isaac Gym Preview 4, but to migrate to:

```text
Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab
Python 3.11
PyTorch 2.7.0+cu128
rsl-rl-lib 3.0.1
```

This is also why the new stack of Isaac Lab is used in the latter part of this chapter.

## VI. Engineering Structure after Isaac Lab Migration

The goal after migration is not to rewrite all physical details, but to preserve the training semantics of HIMLoco as much as possible:

- Unitree A1, 12-dimensional joint position action;
- Action scale `0.25`;
- PD stiffness `40.0`, damping `1.0`;
- `dt=0.005`, decimation `4`, episode length `20s`;
- rough terrain curriculum;
- Command range `x/y = [-1, 1]`, yaw/heading `[-pi, pi]`;
- Policy observation `270`;
- Critic observation `238`;
- HIM runner includes `HIMActorCritic`, `HIMEstimator`, `HIMPPO`.

The local structure of the migrated project is as follows:

```text
HIMLoco/
  source/himloco_isaaclab_tasks/
    himloco_isaaclab_tasks/
      a1/
        rough_env_cfg.py
        agents/rsl_rl_ppo_cfg.py
      rsl_rl_him.py
  scripts/
    isaaclab_train_himloco.py
    train_himloco_isaaclab.sh
    train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh
```

Among them, `rough_env_cfg.py` is responsible for transforming the A1 rough terrain task in Isaac Lab into a HIMLoco-style observation/reward/domain-randomization configuration; `rsl_rl_him.py` adapts the HIM-related algorithms from the original repository to the observation group and TensorDict interface of `rsl-rl-lib 3.x`.

## VII. Environment Preparation

It is recommended to define several path variables first, so as to avoid hardcoding commands on a specific machine:

```bash
export HIMLOCO_ROOT=/path/to/HIMLoco
export ISAACLAB_ROOT=/path/to/IsaacLab
export PYTHON_BIN=/path/to/isaaclab-python/bin/python
```

The key versions of the actual measurement environment in this chapter are as follows:

```text
GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, sm_120
Torch: 2.7.0+cu128
Isaac Sim: 5.1
rsl-rl-lib: 3.0.1
```

The migration task package must be installed in an editable manner:

```bash
cd "$HIMLOCO_ROOT"

"$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip install -e \
  "$HIMLOCO_ROOT/source/himloco_isaaclab_tasks" \
  --no-deps
```

Here, `--no-deps` is used to avoid pip re-parsing the heavy dependencies of Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab. It is best to keep the Isaac environment managed by the existing Isaac Lab environment, and not let a small task package trigger a full reinstall of all dependencies.

## VIII. Checkpoint 1: The ordinary PPO baseline is implemented successfully

After the migration, a normal PPO baseline is retained to confirm that the Isaac Lab task itself is functioning properly:

```bash
cd "$HIMLOCO_ROOT"
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab.sh --num_envs 1 --max_iterations 1
```

When successful, everyone should see a similar output from the observation manager:

```text
Active Observation Terms in Group: 'policy' (shape: (270,))
Active Observation Terms in Group: 'critic' (shape: (238,))
Action Terms (shape: 12)
```

Then the actor/critic structure will be displayed as:

```text
Actor MLP: Linear(in_features=270, ...)
Critic MLP: Linear(in_features=238, ...)
```

The purpose of this baseline is to check whether task registration, environment creation, terrain, reward, observation group, and the rsl-rl 3.x standard runner are functioning properly. It is not a reproduction of the original HIM algorithm, as the actor directly receives the 270-dimensional historical observations without using the 64-dimensional actor input generated by the estimator.

## 9. Checkpoint 2: HIM algorithm smoke test

The reproduction entry that is closer to the original HIMLoco is:

```bash
cd "$HIMLOCO_ROOT"
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh --num_envs 1 --max_iterations 1
```

When successful, everyone should see:

```text
HIMActorCritic ...
Actor MLP: Linear(in_features=64, out_features=512, ...)
Critic MLP: Linear(in_features=238, out_features=512, ...)
Estimator: Linear(in_features=270, out_features=128, ...)
```

This indicates that all three key dimensions are aligned:

| Module | Input Dimension | Output or Purpose |
| :-- | --: | :-- |
| `HIMEstimator` | 270 | Estimates 3-dimensional velocity and 16-dimensional latent values |
| `Actor` | 64 | Outputs a 12-dimensional action |
| `Critic` | 238 | Outputs a value |

The single-environment smoke test can prove that the code flow works, but issues related to batch processing may not be exposed. Therefore, it is recommended to run a smaller-scale debugging test that is closer to the actual training scenario:

```bash
cd "$HIMLOCO_ROOT"
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh --num_envs 64 --max_iterations 2
```

### Checkpoint 3: Record local rendering video

If you want to confirm that the Isaac Lab rendering chain is also working properly, you can start video recording at the HIM training entry point:

```bash
cd "$HIMLOCO_ROOT"
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh \
  --num_envs 4 \
  --max_iterations 2 \
  --video \
  --video_length 120 \
  --video_interval 100000
```

When recording videos, attention should also be paid to the camera position. The migration script defaults to having the viewport camera follow `robot/trunk` in the first environment when `--video` is activated. Otherwise, Isaac Lab may only record a large area of rough terrain and fail to capture the robot dog. `video_interval` should not be set too small either; if recording is triggered for each step, Gymnasium `RecordVideo` will produce many 1-frame clips, which are not suitable for direct use in tutorials.

This video demonstrates that the A1 rough-terrain environment, camera capture, action steps, and training cycles are connected. However, it only has 2 iterations, and the policy has not yet learned to stabilize its gait. Therefore, do not compare it with the final movement results in the official video. The blue and green arrows in the video come from Isaac Lab’s command visualization, used to show speed commands and the current speed direction.

## Ten. Normal Training Entry

If the smoke test passes, you can adjust the number of environments and the number of iterations back to the training scale:

```bash
cd "$HIMLOCO_ROOT"
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh --num_envs 4096 --max_iterations 200000
```

Default log writing:

```text
logs/rsl_rl/himloco_a1_rough_him_isaaclab
```

If it is just continuing the debugging, it is recommended not to run 4096 environments from the start. A more reliable debugging step-by-step is:

```bash
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh --num_envs 1 --max_iterations 1
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh --num_envs 64 --max_iterations 2
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh --num_envs 512 --max_iterations 10
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh --num_envs 4096 --max_iterations 200000
```

At each level, check whether the observation shape is correct, whether NaN occurs in loss values, whether GPU memory is stable, and whether the checkpoint is saved properly. This is easier to identify issues than simply running the training until completion.

## 11. Several boundaries in the migration implementation

Migration is not a line-by-line translation. When replicating, you should know where the alignment is strict and where it is approximate for engineering purposes.

Parts that must be aligned precisely:

- The policy observation dimension remains `270`;
- The critic observation dimension remains `238`;
- The actor input remains `64 = 45 + 3 + 16`;
- A1 action scale, PD gains, dt, decimation, and episode length are aligned;
- PPO hyperparameters are mapped according to the original repository configuration;
- The velocity loss and swap loss of the estimator are retained.

Parts with approximate engineering:

- The external force event in Isaac Lab does not directly expose the `disturbance` buffer of the original `legged_gym`, so the 3 slots for external force in the privileged observation are kept as 0 to maintain a 238-dimensional layout;
- The original repository has special handling for termination privileged observations, and the Isaac Lab migration version uses next critic observation as an approximation;
- The terrain generator, USD assets, and contact naming come from Isaac Lab, not the pixel-by-pixel equivalent scenarios of Isaac Gym Preview 4;
- The smoke test only validates the training process, not the paper metrics or real robot performance.

These boundaries do not affect the core pipeline of learning HIMLoco, but for serious paper reproduction, further long-term training, multiple random seeds, official metric alignment, and real robot deployment verification are required.

## XII. Common Errors and Troubleshooting

### 1. `no kernel image is available for execution on the device`

This is usually because the PyTorch CUDA wheel does not support the current GPU architecture. For Blackwell graphics cards, you need to check:

```bash
"$PYTHON_BIN" - <<'PY'
import torch
print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda)
print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
print(torch.cuda.get_arch_list())
PY
```

If `sm_120` or `compute_120` is not present in the list, the old stack is likely to fail to run. It is recommended to migrate to a wheel that supports Blackwell, such as PyTorch 2.7+ CUDA 12.8.

### 2. Isaac Gym cannot find `libpython3.7m.so.1.0`

This is a common issue in the old Isaac Gym Preview 4. You need to add the `lib` from the conda env to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`:

```bash
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/conda/env/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}
```

However, if everyone has already moved to the new stack of Isaac Lab, this issue usually is no longer a major problem.

### 3. Task registration failed

If the report cannot find `Isaac-HIMLoco-Rough-Unitree-A1-v0`, check first:

```bash
echo "$HIMLOCO_ROOT"
echo "$ISAACLAB_ROOT"
"$PYTHON_BIN" -m pip show himloco_isaaclab_tasks
```

Also confirm that the training script has added the following paths to `sys.path`:

```text
HIMLoco/source/himloco_isaaclab_tasks
IsaacLab/source/isaaclab
IsaacLab/source/isaaclab_tasks
IsaacLab/source/isaaclab_assets
IsaacLab/source/isaaclab_rl
```

### 4. The actor input dimension is not 64

If the actor input printed by the HIM runner is not 64, prioritize checking whether the policy observation remains `45 x 6 = 270`. The default order of the observation history in Isaac Lab is different from that of the old repository. In the migration code, the history needs to be processed in order, and then the current frame's 45-dimensional data is fed into the actor.

### 5. NaN occurs for loss

First, reduce the scale to:

```bash
./scripts/train_himloco_isaaclab_him.sh --num_envs 1 --max_iterations 1
```

After confirming that the observation shape, reward terms, and estimator loss are all normal, gradually increase `num_envs`. If the value is NaN in the 4096 environment from the start, the issue may stem from a certain reset, height scan, terrain, or batch dimension, and it is not easy to identify directly.

## XIII. What should be mastered after completing this chapter

After completing this chapter, everyone should be able to describe the implementation of HIMLoco as a complete pipeline:

```text
Unitree A1 / rough terrain
  -> 并行仿真环境
  -> 45 维 one-step observation
  -> 6 帧历史堆叠成 270 维 policy observation
  -> 238 维 privileged critic observation
  -> HIMEstimator 从历史观测估计 velocity 和 latent
  -> Actor 使用 64 维输入输出 12 维动作
  -> Critic 使用 238 维 privileged observation 估计 value
  -> HIMPPO 同时更新 policy、critic 和 estimator
  -> checkpoint / TensorBoard / 后续 play 或部署
```

More importantly, it should be understood that the engineering core of such quadruped robot reinforcement learning projects is not just “running PPO”. What truly determines the quality of the project is often:

- Which quantities in the observations can be obtained during deployment, and which can only be used during training;
- How historical observations compensate for unobservable states;
- How the privileged critic utilizes simulation true values;
- How domain randomization creates Sim2Real robustness;
- What each of smoke test, debug training, and full training verifies.

These ideas are applicable not only to HIMLoco, but also to many leg-and-foot robots, mobile robots, and simulation-to-reality migration projects.
